ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are AC power supply terminals on the left, and the total power supply voltage is measured by V1 connected across the upper and lower two bus lines. A capacitor C is connected in series in the upper line, and voltmeter V2 is connected across the two ends of the capacitor, so V2 measures the capacitor voltage. The node on the right side of the capacitor is connected downward to a branch composed of resistor R and inductor L connected in series, and voltmeter V3 is connected across the two ends of this R-L series branch, so V3 measures the voltage of the R-L branch. The whole circuit is equivalent to capacitor C connected in series with the R-L series branch, and V1 measures the total voltage. Reasoning: The problem statement gives that the readings of the three voltmeters are all 220 V, so |V_C| = |V_RL| = |V_total| = 220 V. Taking the series current as the reference phasor, the capacitor voltage V_C lags the current by 90°, that is, the direction is -90°; the R-L series branch voltage V_RL leads the current by an angle φ, where tan φ = X_L / R. The total voltage is the phasor sum of V_C and V_RL. The magnitudes of the two partial voltage phasors are equal, and the magnitude of their resultant phasor is also equal to the magnitude of either component; therefore the angle between these two equal-length phasors must be 120°. Since V_C is at -90° and V_RL is at +φ, the angle between the two is φ + 90°. Thus φ + 90° = 120°, giving φ = 30°. Also R = 10√3 Ω, so X_L = R tan 30° = 10√3 × 1/√3 = 10 Ω.

The magnitudes of the two partial voltage phasors are equal, and the magnitude of their resultant phasor is also equal to the magnitude of either component; therefore the angle between these two equal-length phasors must be 120°. Since V_C is at -90° and V_RL is at +φ, the angle between the two is φ + 90°. Thus φ + 90° = 120°, giving φ = 30°. Also R = 10√3 Ω, so X_L = R tan 30° = 10√3 × 1/√3 = 10 Ω.
